root.label: Crown, Church, Parliament
root.gloss: How the Tudor Reformation, Spanish Armada, English Civil War, 1649 Regicide, and 1689 Bill of Rights shifted sovereignty to Parliament.

children.label: Part 1: Tudor Reformation
children.gloss: Henry VIII’s Break with Rome and dissolution of the monasteries, followed by Elizabeth I’s 1559 Middle Way and Catholic plots.

children.label: 1. Reformation & Break with Rome
children.q2Chain: Luther’s Protest & Great Matter → Roman Deadlock & Cromwell Laws → 1534 Supremacy & Monasteries
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Luther’s Protest & Great Matter → Roman Deadlock & Cromwell Laws → 1534 Supremacy & Monasteries.

children.label: Luther’s Protest & Great Matter
children.gloss: Martin Luther’s 1517 protest fractured Christendom before Henry VIII’s lack of a male heir drove him to seek an annulment.

children.label: 1517 Wittenberg 95 Arguments
children.gloss: Attacked corrupt indulgence sales; Henry won Faith Defender title.

children.label: Need for Male Tudor Successor
children.gloss: Catherine bore only Princess Mary; Feared dynastic civil war.

children.label: → Demanded 1527 Papal Annulment
children.gloss: Pursued marriage to Anne Boleyn; Cited Leviticus marriage curse.

children.label: Roman Deadlock & Cromwell Laws
children.gloss: With Pope Clement VII captive to Emperor Charles V, Thomas Cromwell used the Reformation Parliament to sever Roman appeals.

children.label: 1527 Sack of Rome Trapped Pope
children.gloss: Charles V held Clement VII; Catherine was Emperor’s aunt.

children.label: Cromwell’s Parliamentary Statutes
children.gloss: Stopped annates taxes to Rome; 1533 Act banned papal appeals.

children.label: → Wolsey Fell & Anne Crowned
children.gloss: Cranmer voided Aragon marriage; Declared England sovereign realm.

children.label: 1534 Supremacy & Monasteries
children.gloss: The 1534 Act of Supremacy made Henry Supreme Head of the Church of England, followed by closing over 800 monasteries.

children.label: 1534 Act of Royal Supremacy
children.gloss: Made Henry Supreme Church Head; Executed Sir Thomas More.

children.label: Dissolved Over 800 Monasteries
children.gloss: Closed houses from 1536 to 1540; Sold monastic estates to gentry.

children.label: Enriched Crown & Elevated MPs
children.gloss: Ended 1,000 years papal rule; Relied on parliamentary statutes.

children.label: 2. Elizabeth I & The Middle Way
children.q2Chain: 1559 Settlement & Via Media → Northern Earls & 1570 Papal Bull → Babington Plot & Mary Executed
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1559 Settlement & Via Media → Northern Earls & 1570 Papal Bull → Babington Plot & Mary Executed.

children.label: 1559 Settlement & Via Media
children.gloss: Inheriting Marian trauma, Elizabeth established her 1559 Protestant Middle Way as Supreme Governor with an English Prayer Book.

children.label: Marian Burnings & Puritan Return
children.gloss: Nearly 300 Protestants burned; Exiled Calvinists urged reform.

children.label: 1559 Supreme Governor Compromise
children.gloss: Calmed moderate Catholic subjects; Sacked refusing Marian bishops.

children.label: 1559 Uniformity & 12d Recusancy
children.gloss: Shared English Common Prayer Book; Avoided windows into men’s souls.

children.label: Northern Earls & 1570 Papal Bull
children.gloss: Following the 1569 Northern Earls’ rebellion, Pope Pius V excommunicated Elizabeth in 1570, turning Catholics into suspects.

children.label: 1569 Northern Earls Rebellion
children.gloss: Held Mass in Durham Cathedral; Elizabeth executed 400 rebels.

children.label: 1570 Bull Regnans in Excelsis
children.gloss: Pope Pius V excommunicated Queen; Released Catholics from allegiance.

children.label: → Cast Loyal Catholics as Traitors
children.gloss: Fuelled covert assassination plots; Hardened state anti-Catholic laws.

children.label: Babington Plot & Mary Executed
children.gloss: Walsingham’s spies broke ciphered beer-barrel letters in the 1586 Babington Plot, leading to Mary Stuart’s execution in 1587.

children.label: Walsingham Cracked Beer Ciphers
children.gloss: Intercepted 1586 Babington plot; Proved Mary backed assassination.

children.label: Feb 1587 Fotheringhay Execution
children.gloss: Elizabeth signed death warrant; Removed Catholic rival claimant.

children.label: → Triggered 1588 Spanish Armada
children.gloss: Infuriated Catholic Philip II; Gave papal blessing to invade.

children.label: Part 2: Armada & Stuart Crisis
children.gloss: The defeat of the 1588 Spanish Armada, followed by Charles I’s Personal Rule, Civil War, 1649 Regicide, and 1689 Bill of Rights.

children.label: 3. Spanish Armada & Naval War
children.q2Chain: Catholic Crusade & Cadiz Raid → Channel Chase & Calais Fireships → Gravelines & Protestant Wind
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Catholic Crusade & Cadiz Raid → Channel Chase & Calais Fireships → Gravelines & Protestant Wind.

children.label: Catholic Crusade & Cadiz Raid
children.gloss: Provoked by Dutch aid, piracy, and Mary’s execution, Philip II’s fleet suffered a year’s delay from Drake’s 1587 Cadiz raid.

children.label: Dutch Aid, Drake & Mary’s Death
children.gloss: Backed Dutch Protestant rebels; Drake raided Caribbean silver.

children.label: April 1587 Raid on Cadiz
children.gloss: Destroyed thirty Spanish warships; Burned seasoned barrel staves.

children.label: → Delayed Fleet & Spoiled Water
children.gloss: Held Armada back one full year; Green casks rotted ship rations.

children.label: Held Armada back one full year
children.gloss: Held Armada back one full year

children.label: Channel Chase & Calais Fireships
children.gloss: English race-built galleons harassed Medina Sidonia’s 130-ship crescent before eight midnight fireships scattered it off Calais.

children.label: 130-Ship Crescent vs Culverins
children.gloss: Hawkins built fast galleons; Long-range brass culverin guns.

children.label: Eight Midnight Calais Fireships
children.gloss: Packed with pitch and gunpowder; Struck vulnerable Calais anchorage.

children.label: → Cut Cables & Broke Crescent
children.gloss: Spanish scattered into North Sea; Prevented Parma Flanders linkup.

children.label: Gravelines & Protestant Wind
children.gloss: Battered at Gravelines and driven around Scotland and Ireland by fierce Atlantic storms, only 67 Spanish ships returned.

children.label: Close-Range Gravelines Broadsides
children.gloss: Smashed scattered wooden hulls; Drove battered fleet northward.

children.label: Atlantic Gales & Irish Wrecks
children.gloss: Storms wrecked dozens on rocks; Only 67 damaged ships returned.

children.label: Cemented Naval Protestant Pride
children.gloss: Struck God blew Armada medal; Secured English independence.

children.label: 4. Civil War, Regicide & 1689
children.q2Chain: Personal Rule & Five MPs Raid → Naseby & Regicide of Charles I → Glorious Revolution & 1689 Bill
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Personal Rule & Five MPs Raid → Naseby & Regicide of Charles I → Glorious Revolution & 1689 Bill.

children.label: Personal Rule & Five MPs Raid
children.gloss: Charles I’s eleven-year Personal Rule, inland Ship Money, and armed 1642 raid on Five MPs plunged England into civil war.

children.label: 11-Year Rule & Ship Money Tax
children.gloss: Ruled 1629–40 without Parliament; John Hampden refused inland tax.

children.label: 4 Jan 1642 Raid on Five MPs
children.gloss: 400 armed guards entered Commons; Five MPs fled by river boat.

children.label: Five MPs fled by river boat
children.gloss: Five MPs fled by river boat

children.label: → Triggered Aug 1642 Civil War
children.gloss: Charles fled capital to north; Raised royal flag at Nottingham.

children.label: Naseby & Regicide of Charles I
children.gloss: Defeated by the New Model Army at Naseby in 1645, Charles I was tried after Pride’s Purge and beheaded in January 1649.

children.label: June 1645 New Model Naseby Win
children.gloss: Merit-promoted paid redcoat army; Fairfax and Cromwell routed King.

children.label: Pride’s Purge & Treason Trial
children.gloss: Army expelled moderate MPs; Rump tried Charles for treason.

children.label: → 30 Jan 1649 Whitehall Regicide
children.gloss: Publicly beheaded Charles I; Established republican rule.

children.label: Glorious Revolution & 1689 Bill
children.gloss: After Catholic James II fled in 1688, William and Mary accepted the 1689 Bill of Rights, binding monarchy under Parliament.

children.label: 1688 Flight of King James II
children.gloss: Dutch army landed at Torbay; Catholic James II fled to France.

children.label: Catholic James II fled to France
children.gloss: Catholic James II fled to France

children.label: 1689 Statutory Bill of Rights
children.gloss: Crowned William III and Mary II; Barred taxes without MP votes.

children.label: Crowned William III and Mary II
children.gloss: Crowned William III and Mary II

children.label: Forged Constitutional Monarchy
children.gloss: Stopped kings cancelling statutes; Bound Crown permanently to law.

children.label: Part 3: Shifting Sovereignty
children.gloss: Evaluating which turning point across 1517–1689 shifted supreme power most decisively from absolute monarchs to Parliament.

children.label: 5. Shifting Sovereign Power
children.q2Chain: Tudor King-in-Parliament → Stuart Absolutism & Regicide → 1689 Parliamentary Supremacy
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Tudor King-in-Parliament → Stuart Absolutism & Regicide → 1689 Parliamentary Supremacy.

children.label: Tudor King-in-Parliament
children.gloss: Henry VIII and Elizabeth I used parliamentary statutes for religious change, elevating MPs into legislative partners.

children.label: Reformation Passed by Statute
children.gloss: Ended Roman power through MPs; Monastic lands bound local gentry.

children.label: Elizabethan Patriotic Unity
children.gloss: 1559 Settlement calmed divisions; 1588 Armada fused faith and nation.

children.label: → Created King-in-Parliament
children.gloss: Religious shifts needed MP votes; Grew Commons institutional confidence.

children.label: Stuart Absolutism & Regicide
children.gloss: Stuart Divine Right claims shattered Tudor partnership, culminating in Naseby, Pride’s Purge, and the 1649 execution of Charles I.

children.label: Divine Right & Scottish Revolt
children.gloss: Claimed kings answered to God; 1640 Scots war broke finances.

children.label: 1649 Judicial Regicide Shock
children.gloss: Abolished monarchy and Lords; Created republican Commonwealth.

children.label: Shattered Royal Inviolability
children.gloss: Held anointed king to treason law; Proved power came from people.

children.label: Held anointed king to treason law
children.gloss: Held anointed king to treason law

children.label: 1689 Parliamentary Supremacy
children.gloss: The 1689 Bill of Rights permanently ended absolute royal prerogative, enthroning supreme parliamentary authority.

children.label: 1689 Binding Statutory Contract
children.gloss: Removed royal veto over statutes; Banned unvoted royal taxation.

children.label: Completed 170-Year Power Shift
children.gloss: Ended absolute divine-right rule; Enthroned parliamentary supremacy.

children.label: 1649 Blade vs 1689 Statute
children.gloss: 1649 republic proved temporary; 1689 law permanently bound kings.
